messages:
alex_ruiz: Heads up — noticed a perf regression on Mistral-22B AWQ yesterday during load test. Throughput dropped ~28% at 1k seq vs baseline. Root cause looks like kernel fallback + KV thrash.

mira_shah: ugh. any trace/prof output?

alex_ruiz: posted profile snippets below. main symptom: near-seq 512->1024 we start hitting a path that chooses a fallback matmul kernel instead of flash_attn for attention, and KV cache evictions spike. sample flame: `cpu:io 6% | gpu:compute 68% | wait:26%`

tony_nguyen: can you paste the kernel chooser log? iirc we log heuristic decisions.

alex_ruiz: sure — snippet: ```
[kernel-chooser] model=Mistral-22B arch=decoder-only seq=1024 head_dim=128 heads=64 dtype=awq_int8
selected_kernel=matmul_fallback reason=rope_scale_mismatch + small_block_align
fallback_history=[flash_attn_fail(oom), matmul_fast(use)]
```

mira_shah: rope_scale_mismatch? that suggests RoPE scaling code path thinks tokens require a different rotary factor. did quantization change the dtype path?

jia_wu: AWQ per-channel ranges sometimes shift effective scale slightly compared to GPTQ; that could move some multihead GEMM into unaligned block sizes and disable our optimized kernel. Also FP8 experiments we ran earlier changed some kernel probing order.

tony_nguyen: any accuracy delta on calibration prompts? we should compare AWQ vs GPTQ on the same calibration set.

alex_ruiz: ran quick eval: calibration prompts (n=200) error delta: AWQ - GPTQ = +0.8% token-level mismatch (GPTQ better). For some RoPE-sensitive tasks (date math, long-context quotes) mismatch up to 2.4%.

mira_shah: hmm that could explain the chooser: we added an extra validation check — if RoPE checksum != expected then fallback to safer matmul to avoid divergence. That buys correctness but kills perf.

perf-bot: autotune report available: job#8734 — best kernels: flash_attn (seq<=512), block_attn_v2 (seq 513-896), matmul (>=897) for dtype=float16. AWQ_int8 path currently forced matmul at >=768.

tony_nguyen: we need to decide tradeoffs: revert RoPE checksum gating for AWQ path? or improve RoPE-calibration to reduce false positives.

alex_ruiz: proposal: 1) add a permissive threshold for RoPE checksum for AWQ (allow small diffs), 2) add a short-lived KV cache warm window to avoid evict thrash when switching kernels, 3) run a focused batch of calibration prompts under AWQ w/ FP8 fallback disabled.

jia_wu: +1 for permissive checksum but only if we add offline regression checks. I can run a controlled sweep: AWQ calib prompts across 5 seeds, measure per-prompt delta; if delta<1.2% keep permissive.

mira_shah: for KV cache warm window — we could pin first N requests to previous kernel for T ms to stabilize caches. but that complicates routing and makes latency SLO trickier. alternative: pre-populate KV for the chosen kernel by running a micro-batch through the chosen kernel before real traffic.

tony_nguyen: pre-population sounds safer. Implementation: when kernel changes, enqueue a micro-batch of size min(16, pending) with synthetic prefixes used during profiling. Should be quick.

alex_ruiz: also saw a weird head-dim misalignment warning in logs: `head_dim % 32 != 0 -> fallback` for AWQ path. That one is purely alignment/packing. Might be from our quantization packing rounding.

jia_wu: AWQ packing currently packs to 16-byte lanes; some head_dim combos (like 119->128 rounding) push block size mismatch. We can change packer to zero-pad to next multiple of 32 for kernels that require it. Trade: +memory overhead vs avoid fallback.

mira_shah: ok action list?

alex_ruiz: 1) Jia: run AWQ calibration sweep (n=5) and report token-delta matrix by EOD (TS 1860001300). 2) Tony: prototype micro-batch pre-population for kernel switch in runtime (PR) — aim for small canary by tomorrow. 3) Mira: adjust kernel-chooser to allow permissive RoPE threshold behind a feature flag and add logging. 4) Ops: schedule a canary with Mistral-22B AWQ on a dedicated pool (low QPS) to measure throughput and accuracy.

mira_shah: noted. I'll add the feature flag: `runtime.experimental.permissive_rope_awq=true` and wire extra logging.

tony_nguyen: i'll start the pre-pop PR. rough plan: detect kernel change -> run prepop task async -> delay new-requests-routing by up to 25ms if prepop pending. we can tune later.

jia_wu: starting calib sweep now. will upload results to /mnt/prof/awq_calib/1860001234/ and post csv.

perf-bot: perf trace: /traces/1860001234/summary.html (attached)

alex_ruiz: quick notes on metrics to watch during canary: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, avg kernel-switches/min, KV-evictions/sec, per-prompt token-delta. Also watch GPU SM occupancy and pcie stalls.

mira_shah: one more thought — FP8 path we trialed changed kernel probing order: it tried block_attn_v2 later which might exacerbate fallback at 768-896. For canary we should lock kernel probe order to the stable sequence.

alex_ruiz: agreed. lock probe order for canary to: flash_attn -> block_attn_v2 -> block_attn_v1 -> matmul.

tony_nguyen: if micro-pop reduces cold evictions we should see throughput recover to within 5% of baseline. if not, revert permissive RoPE.

jia_wu: calib done — uploading csv now. summary: mean token-delta AWQ vs GPTQ = 0.96% (std 0.4). 3 prompts >2% (RoPE heavy). attaching sample diffs in csv.

alex_ruiz: that looks acceptable for permissive threshold 1.5%. Mira, set threshold to 1.5% and enable flag in canary.

mira_shah: done — flag enabled on canary cluster.

perf-bot: canary started at 1860001350: 100qps steady for 10m. initial readouts: tokens/sec +24% vs previous run at same QPS, p95 latency +8ms. kernel-switches/min dropped from 6->1. KV-evictions/sec down 78%.

alex_ruiz: amazing. looks like pre-pop + permissive RoPE did the trick. let's let it run for an hour and then roll to wider test.

tony_nguyen: i'll open PR with micro-pop and probe-order lock. tagging @mira_shah and @jia_wu for review.

mira_shah: thanks all. we'll monitor regressions and keep the feature flag gated until next release. :thumbsup:

alex_ruiz: nice teamwork. closing thread after wider rollout.
